title: Genesis 9 — The covenant, the bow in the cloud, and Noah's vineyard

paragraphs.text: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־נֹ֖חַ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The Elohim blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them: be fruitful and multiply and fill the land.
i18n.he: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־נֹ֖חַ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Die Elohim segneten Noah und seine Söhne und sprachen zu ihnen: Seid fruchtbar und mehrt euch und füllt das Land.
i18n.es: Los Elohim bendijeron a Noé y a sus hijos, y les dijeron: sed fecundos y multiplicaos y llenad la tierra.
i18n.fr: Les Elohim bénirent Noé et ses fils, et leur dirent : soyez féconds, multipliez-vous et remplissez la terre.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはノアとその息子たちを祝福して、彼らに言われた、「実を結び、増えよ、そして地に満ちよ。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 노아와 그의 아들들을 축복하고 그들에게 말씀하셨다: 번성하고 번식하여 땅을 채우라.
i18n.ru: И благословили Элохим Ноя и сыновей его и сказали им: плодитесь и умножайтесь и наполните землю.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音赐福给挪亚和他的众子，对他们说：要多产繁衍，遍满大地。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音祝福挪亞和他的兒子們，對他們說：要生養眾多，遍滿大地。

notes.official:
**The Genesis 1 blessing, re-issued.** Word-for-word, this is the blessing of 1:28 — *peru u-revu u-mil'u et ha-aretz* — spoken now to the survivors at the start of the second human age. The chapter is doing the structural thing it has been doing since chapter 8: rebooting Genesis 1's grammar onto the post-Flood world. Adam and his wife received this blessing as the first humans; Noah and his sons receive it again as the second-first humans. The Flood narrative has positioned Noah as a second Adam — same blessing, same mandate.

What is missing is also revealing. Genesis 1:28 included *kivshuha* (subdue it) and *redu* (rule over). Here those verbs are dropped — only the demographic command (*be fruitful, multiply, fill*) is preserved. The dominion mandate is being reissued separately in v2 with new and harsher vocabulary.

paragraphs.text: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כָּל־חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: The dread of you and the terror of you shall be upon every living thing of the land, and upon every bird of the skies — upon everything that the soil teems with, and upon all the fish of the sea: into your hand they are given.
i18n.he: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כָּל־חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃
i18n.de: Die Furcht und der Schrecken vor euch soll auf jedem Lebendigen des Landes liegen und auf jedem Vogel der Himmel — auf allem, wovon der Boden wimmelt, und auf allen Fischen des Meeres: In eure Hand sind sie gegeben.
i18n.es: El temor y el pavor de vosotros estarán sobre todo ser viviente de la tierra, y sobre toda ave de los cielos—sobre todo lo que pulula el suelo, y sobre todos los peces del mar: en vuestra mano son entregados.
i18n.fr: La crainte et la terreur de vous seront sur tout être vivant de la terre, et sur tout oiseau des cieux — sur tout ce dont le sol fourmille, et sur tous les poissons de la mer : ils sont livrés entre vos mains.
i18n.ja: お前たちへの恐れと、お前たちへのおののきは、地のすべての生けるものの上に、また天のすべての鳥の上にあるであろう——土に群がるすべてのもの、海のすべての魚の上にも。これらはお前たちの手に渡されている。
i18n.ko: 너희에 대한 두려움과 너희에 대한 공포가 땅의 모든 산 것 위에, 그리고 하늘의 모든 새 위에 — 흙이 떼지어 내는 모든 것 위에, 그리고 바다의 모든 물고기 위에 임할 것이다: 그것들이 너희 손에 넘겨졌다.
i18n.ru: Страх перед вами и трепет перед вами да будет на всяком живом существе земли и на всякой птице небесной — на всём, чем кишит почва, и на всех рыбах моря: в вашу руку они отданы.
i18n.zh: 大地一切活物，诸天的一切飞鸟——土地上群集的一切，以及海中一切的鱼——都要惧怕你们、畏惧你们：它们都交在你们手中。
i18n.zh-Hant: 大地上一切活物、諸天中一切飛鳥—凡土壤所滋生的，以及海中一切的魚，都必對你們感到畏懼和恐怖：牠們都交在你們手中。

notes.official:
**The dominion mandate, re-issued in fear-vocabulary.** Where Genesis 1:28 told the first humans to *rule* (*radah*) and *subdue* (*kavash*) the animals — verbs of governance and ordering — the post-Flood mandate uses *mora* (dread) and *chittah* (terror). These are war-vocabulary words. *Mora* appears in Deuteronomy and the conquest narratives for the dread that falls on Israel's enemies (Deut 11:25, 'no man shall be able to stand before you; YHWH your Elohim will lay the dread of you'). *Chittah* (from חתת *chatat* — to be shattered, broken) names the way enemies *collapse* in fear (Job 6:21).

The rhetorical move is precise. Before the Flood, animal and human relations are pictured under the verbs *radah* and *kavash* — verbs that have a meaning-range from 'rule' (functional) to 'tread down' (forceful), but which name a *relationship*. After the Flood, the relationship is named by the *psychological state* the animals will live in: dread, terror. The next verse explains why.

paragraphs.text: כָּל־רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָ֑ה כְּיֶ֣רֶק עֵ֔שֶׂב נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־כֹּֽל׃

i18n.en: Every moving thing that lives shall be yours for food; as the green plants, I have given you everything.
i18n.he: כָּל־רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָ֑ה כְּיֶ֣רֶק עֵ֔שֶׂב נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־כֹּֽל׃
i18n.de: Jedes sich regende Lebendige soll euch zur Speise sein; wie das grüne Kraut, gebe ich euch alles.
i18n.es: Todo lo que se mueve y vive os será para alimento; como las plantas verdes, os he dado todo.
i18n.fr: Tout ce qui se meut et qui a vie vous servira de nourriture ; comme la verdure des plantes, je vous donne tout.
i18n.ja: 命を有して動くすべてのものは、お前たちの食物となるであろう。緑の草と同様に、わたしはお前たちにすべてを与える。
i18n.ko: 살아있는 모든 움직이는 것이 너희에게 양식이 될 것이다; 푸른 채소처럼, 내가 너희에게 모든 것을 주었다.
i18n.ru: Всё движущееся, что живёт, будет вам в пищу; как зелень травную, я отдал вам всё.
i18n.zh: 凡活着的一切动物，都可作你们的食物；正如青菜一样，我都赐给你们了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 凡活著的動物都可作你們的食物；正如綠色的植物，我都已賜給你們。

notes.official:
**Meat enters the human diet.** This verse is the precise inverse of 1:29–30. There, the first humans were given *every herb yielding seed* and *every tree with seed-bearing fruit* — and only that — as food; the animals likewise received only the green plants. The Edenic and antediluvian diet, on the chapter's own account, is vegetarian.

Here, post-Flood, the dietary permission is expanded: *kol remes asher hu-chai lakhem yihyeh l'akhlah* — *every moving thing that lives shall be yours for food*. The comparative phrase *k-yereq esev* (*as the green plants*) makes the analogy explicit: meat is now given on the same footing that vegetation was given in 1:29. Two ages of human diet, with the Flood as the hinge.

The chapter's editorial logic seems to be: the violent world of chapter 6 (where 'all flesh had corrupted its way upon the land,' 6:12) is being acknowledged. Pure herbivory was the Edenic ideal; in the post-Flood, post-violence world, the chapter concedes meat-eating — but with the immediate restrictions of vv. 4–6.

paragraphs.text: אַךְ־בָּשָׂ֕ר בְּנַפְשׁ֥וֹ דָמ֖וֹ לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: Only — flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.
i18n.he: אַךְ־בָּשָׂ֕ר בְּנַפְשׁ֥וֹ דָמ֖וֹ לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
i18n.de: Nur — Fleisch mit seinem Leben, seinem Blut, sollt ihr nicht essen.
i18n.es: Solo—carne con su vida, su sangre, no comeréis.
i18n.fr: Seulement — la chair avec sa vie, c'est-à-dire son sang, vous n'en mangerez pas.
i18n.ja: ただし——その命、すなわち血を有する肉を、お前たちは食べてはならない。
i18n.ko: 오직 — 그 생명, 곧 그 피가 있는 육신은 너희가 먹지 말아야 한다.
i18n.ru: Только плоти с её жизнью, с её кровью, не ешьте.
i18n.zh: 只是——带着生命，就是带血的肉，你们不可吃。
i18n.zh-Hant: 只是—帶著生命的肉，就是牠的血，你們不可吃。

notes.official:
**The blood-life equation.** The Hebrew is densely compressed: *basar b'nafsho damo lo tokhelu* — literally *flesh in-its-nefesh its-blood, you shall not eat*. The blood is in apposition to *nefesh* (life-soul, breath-self); the chapter is asserting an identification, not a separate rule. The blood IS the nefesh, the carrier of the life-force.

This is the first explicit dietary prohibition in the Torah. It is repeated and elaborated in Leviticus 17:10–14 ('the *nefesh* of the flesh is in the blood'), Deuteronomy 12:23 ('the blood is the *nefesh*, and you shall not eat the *nefesh* with the flesh'), and underlies all kosher slaughter regulations (shechitah's central concern is the complete drainage of blood). The chapter is establishing the principle that grounds an entire later legal tradition.

The theological logic, on the chapter's terms: meat is permitted, but the *life-force* in the meat must be returned (poured out, drained) and not consumed. To consume the blood would be to consume the *nefesh* of the animal — a kind of category-violation that the chapter prohibits even as it concedes the meat itself.

paragraphs.text: וְאַ֨ךְ אֶת־דִּמְכֶ֤ם לְנַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ אֶדְרֹ֔שׁ מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־חַיָּ֖ה אֶדְרְשֶׁ֑נּוּ וּמִיַּ֣ד הָֽאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ הָֽאָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: And further — your own blood, for your lives, I will demand; from the hand of every living thing I will demand it, and from the hand of the human, from the hand of each man's brother, I will demand the life of the human.
i18n.he: וְאַ֨ךְ אֶת־דִּמְכֶ֤ם לְנַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ אֶדְרֹ֔שׁ מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־חַיָּ֖ה אֶדְרְשֶׁ֑נּוּ וּמִיַּ֣ד הָֽאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ הָֽאָדָֽם׃
i18n.de: Und ferner — euer eigenes Blut, für euer Leben, werde ich fordern; von der Hand jedes Lebendigen werde ich es fordern, und von der Hand des Menschen, von der Hand des Bruders eines jeden, werde ich das Leben des Menschen fordern.
i18n.es: Y además—vuestra propia sangre, por vuestras vidas, demandaré; de la mano de todo ser viviente la demandaré, y de la mano del ser humano, de la mano del hermano de cada hombre, demandaré la vida del ser humano.
i18n.fr: Et de plus — votre propre sang, pour vos vies, je le redemanderai ; de la main de tout être vivant je le redemanderai, et de la main de l'être humain, de la main du frère de chacun, je redemanderai la vie de l'être humain.
i18n.ja: さらに——お前たち自身の血、お前たちの命については、わたしはこれを問い求める。すべての生けるものの手から、わたしはこれを問い求め、また人の手から、各人の兄弟の手から、わたしは人の命を問い求める。
i18n.ko: 더 나아가 — 너희 자신의 피를, 너희 생명을 위하여, 내가 요구하리라; 모든 산 것의 손에서 내가 그것을 요구하겠고, 사람의 손에서, 각 사람의 형제의 손에서, 내가 사람의 생명을 요구하리라.
i18n.ru: А ещё — крови вашей, за ваши жизни, я взыщу; от руки всякого живого взыщу её, и от руки человека, от руки брата каждого мужа, взыщу жизнь человека.
i18n.zh: 并且——你们自己的血，就是你们的生命，我必追讨；从一切活物的手中我必追讨；从人的手中，从各人弟兄的手中，我必追讨人的生命。
i18n.zh-Hant: 並且—你們自己的血，為你們的生命，我必追討；從一切活物的手中我必追討；從人的手中、從各人弟兄的手中，我必追討人的生命。

notes.official:
**The reckoning for human blood.** The verb *darash* (to seek, inquire, demand) is the chapter's strongest word for divine accountability. The construction *edrosh* — *edreshennu* — *edrosh* (three repetitions in one verse) gives the line its weight: *I will demand, I will demand it, I will demand*. The triple emphasis pivots from animal predation (animals that kill humans will be held to account, v5a) to human violence (humans who kill humans will be held to account, v5b).

The phrase *mi-yad ish achiv* — *from the hand of each man's brother* — is a deliberate echo of chapter 4. Cain killed Hevel his *brother* and YHWH said *the blood of your brother cries out to me from the ground* (4:10). The chapter is invoking that scene by name. The first-recorded fratricide was met then with a curse and a mark; now, after the Flood that the human violence of chapter 6 helped trigger, the chapter installs a *standing* divine demand against brother-killing-brother.

paragraphs.text: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הָֽאָדָ֔ם בָּֽאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ כִּ֚י בְּצֶ֣לֶם אֱלֹהִ֔ים עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: One who sheds the blood of the human — by the human his blood shall be shed; for in the image of the Elohim, they made the human.
i18n.he: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הָֽאָדָ֔ם בָּֽאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ כִּ֚י בְּצֶ֣לֶם אֱלֹהִ֔ים עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָֽם׃
i18n.de: Wer das Blut des Menschen vergießt — durch den Menschen soll sein Blut vergossen werden; denn im Bilde der Elohim machten sie den Menschen.
i18n.es: Quien derrame la sangre del ser humano—por el ser humano será derramada su sangre; pues a imagen de los Elohim, hicieron al ser humano.
i18n.fr: Qui verse le sang de l'être humain — par l'être humain son sang sera versé ; car à l'image des Elohim, ils ont fait l'être humain.
i18n.ja: 人の血を流す者は——人によってその血が流されるであろう。なぜなら、エロヒムの似姿に、彼らは人を造ったからである。
i18n.ko: 사람의 피를 흘리는 자는 — 사람에 의하여 그의 피가 흘려지리라; 엘로힘의 형상으로, 그들이 사람을 만들었기 때문이다.
i18n.ru: Кто прольёт кровь человека — человеком кровь его прольётся; ибо по образу Элохим сделали они человека.
i18n.zh: 凡流人血的——他的血也必由人所流；因为厄罗音是按厄罗音的形象造了人。
i18n.zh-Hant: 凡流人血的—他的血也必由人流出；因為厄羅音是按自己的形像造了人。

notes.official:
**Murder is a wound to the Elohim's likeness.** The verse is structured as a tight chiasm: *shofech / dam / ha-adam / ba-adam / damo / yishshafekh* — *sheds / blood / of-the-human / by-the-human / his-blood / shall-be-shed*. Six words mirroring around their center, with the act and its consequence locked in formal symmetry.

The grounding clause is the load-bearing one for the chapter's anthropology: *ki b'tselem Elohim asah et ha-adam* — *for in the image of the Elohim, he made the human*. This is the third invocation of *tselem Elohim* in Genesis (1:26–27, 5:1, now 9:6) and the only one that draws a *legal* consequence. Killing a human is now framed as an injury to the resemblance the human carries.

On the WoH frame: the *tselem* and *demut* of 1:26 are read as physical resemblance, not metaphor. Here that reading does not weaken — it strengthens — the prohibition. To kill a human is to destroy a body that physically resembles the Elohim who made it. The chapter is not arguing from a 'dignity' that is symbolic or abstract; it is arguing from a literal resemblance that grounds a literal claim. The post-Flood legal order is being founded on the fact that humans look like the Elohim.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתֶּ֖ם פְּר֣וּ וּרְב֑וּ שִׁרְצ֥וּ בָאָ֖רֶץ וּרְבוּ־בָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: As for you — be fruitful and multiply, teem upon the land, and multiply in it.
i18n.he: וְאַתֶּ֖ם פְּר֣וּ וּרְב֑וּ שִׁרְצ֥וּ בָאָ֖רֶץ וּרְבוּ־בָֽהּ׃
i18n.de: Ihr aber — seid fruchtbar und mehrt euch, wimmelt auf dem Land und mehrt euch darin.
i18n.es: Y vosotros—sed fecundos y multiplicaos, pululad sobre la tierra, y multiplicaos en ella.
i18n.fr: Quant à vous — soyez féconds et multipliez-vous, foisonnez sur la terre, et multipliez-vous en elle.
i18n.ja: お前たちについては——実を結び、増え、地に群がり、その中で増えよ」。
i18n.ko: 너희로 말하면 — 번성하고 번식하라, 땅에서 떼지어 다니며, 그 안에서 번식하라.
i18n.ru: А вы — плодитесь и умножайтесь, кишите на земле и умножайтесь на ней.
i18n.zh: 至于你们——要多产繁衍，在大地上群集，在其中繁衍。
i18n.zh-Hant: 至於你們—要生養眾多，在大地上群集繁衍，並在其中增多。

notes.official: The blessing of v1 is restated, and intensified with a new verb: *shirtzu* — **teem, swarm** — the word used in 1:20 of the waters swarming with living creatures, now turned on humankind. After the near-total erasure, the charge to repopulate is urgent, almost biological: not merely "multiply" but "swarm". The repetition brackets vv. 1–7, opening and closing the re-commissioning of humanity with the same command to fill the emptied land.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־נֹ֔חַ וְאֶל־בָּנָ֥יו אִתּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: The Elohim said to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־נֹ֔חַ וְאֶל־בָּנָ֥יו אִתּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sprachen zu Noah und zu seinen Söhnen mit ihm und sagten:
i18n.es: Los Elohim dijeron a Noé y a sus hijos con él, diciendo:
i18n.fr: Les Elohim dirent à Noé et à ses fils avec lui, en disant :
i18n.ja: エロヒムはノアと彼と共にいる息子たちに語って言われた、
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 노아와 그와 함께한 그의 아들들에게 말씀하시며 이르셨다:
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим Ною и сыновьям его с ним, говоря:
i18n.zh: 厄罗音对挪亚和与他同在的众子说：
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音對挪亞和與他同在的兒子們說：

paragraphs.text: וַאֲנִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י מֵקִ֛ים אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם אַֽחֲרֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: As for me — here I am, establishing my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
i18n.he: וַאֲנִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י מֵקִ֛ים אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם אַֽחֲרֵיכֶֽם׃
i18n.de: Ich aber — siehe, ich richte meinen Bund auf mit euch und mit eurem Samen nach euch,
i18n.es: En cuanto a mí—he aquí, establezco mi pacto con vosotros, y con vuestra descendencia después de vosotros,
i18n.fr: Quant à moi — me voici, j'établis mon alliance avec vous, et avec votre descendance après vous,
i18n.ja: 「わたしについては——見よ、わたしはお前たちと、またお前たちの後の子孫と、私の契約を立てる。
i18n.ko: 나로 말하면 — 보라, 내가 너희와, 너희 후의 너희 자손과 내 언약을 세우니,
i18n.ru: А я — вот, я устанавливаю мой завет с вами и с потомством вашим после вас,
i18n.zh: 至于我——看哪，我与你们立我的约，并与你们以后的后裔，
i18n.zh-Hant: 至於我—看哪，我要與你們和你們以後的後裔立我的約，

notes.official:
**The first explicit covenant in the Torah.** *Brit* was first promised to Noah in 6:18 (*and I will establish my brit with you*); here it is enacted. The verb is *meqim* — *establishing*, from קוּם *qum* (to rise, stand). A *brit* is not declared; it is *raised up* between parties, like a structure being set in place.

What is novel is the scope. The chapter will widen it in v10: this brit is not only with humans but with *every living nefesh* aboard the ark — birds, cattle, every wild animal. The chapter is establishing the first universal cosmic covenant, addressed to all life. The later Abrahamic covenant (chapters 15, 17) and the Sinaitic covenant (Exodus 19–24) will both be narrower in scope: a single family, a single people. The Noahic covenant is the canopy under which the rest sit.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־נֶ֤פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֔ם בָּע֧וֹף בַּבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ אִתְּכֶ֑ם מִכֹּל֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י הַתֵּבָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: and with every living being that is with you — among the birds, among the cattle, and among every wild creature of the land that is with you; all of them that came out of the ark, every living thing of the land.
i18n.he: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־נֶ֤פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֔ם בָּע֧וֹף בַּבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ אִתְּכֶ֑ם מִכֹּל֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י הַתֵּבָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: und mit jedem lebenden Wesen, das bei euch ist — unter den Vögeln, unter dem Vieh und unter jedem Wildtier des Landes, das bei euch ist; mit allen, die aus der Arche gekommen sind, mit jedem Lebendigen des Landes.
i18n.es: y con todo ser viviente que está con vosotros—entre las aves, entre el ganado, y entre toda criatura salvaje de la tierra que está con vosotros; todos los que salieron del arca, todo ser viviente de la tierra.
i18n.fr: et avec tout être vivant qui est avec vous — parmi les oiseaux, parmi le bétail, et parmi toute créature sauvage de la terre qui est avec vous ; tous ceux qui sont sortis de l'arche, tout être vivant de la terre.
i18n.ja: また、お前たちと共にいるすべての生ける者——鳥のうち、家畜のうち、お前たちと共にいる地のすべての野の獣のうち——箱舟から出たすべて、地のすべての生けるものと。
i18n.ko: 그리고 너희와 함께한 모든 산 존재와 — 새들 가운데서, 가축 가운데서, 너희와 함께한 땅의 모든 들짐승 가운데서; 방주에서 나온 그들 모두와, 땅의 모든 산 것과.
i18n.ru: и со всяким живым существом, что с вами — среди птиц, среди скота, и среди всякого дикого зверя земли, который с вами; со всеми вышедшими из ковчега, со всяким живым земли.
i18n.zh: 并与你们一同的一切有生命之物——飞鸟、牲畜，以及与你们一同的大地一切野兽；凡从方舟里出来的，大地一切活物。
i18n.zh-Hant: 並與一切與你們同在的生物—飛鳥、牲畜、與你們同在的一切大地上的野生動物；凡從方舟出來的，大地上的一切生物。

notes.official: **A covenant that includes the animals.** The *brit* is drawn not only with Noah and his offspring but with *every living being* that came out of the ark — birds, cattle, wild creatures — and, in v13, with *the land* itself. This is the widest party-list of any covenant in the Hebrew Bible: the later covenants (Abraham, Sinai, David) are with a person, a people, a dynasty, but the Noahic *brit* is cosmic, binding the deity to all flesh and to the earth. The point is repeated across vv. 10–17 ("every living being" / "all flesh") so that it cannot be missed — what is guaranteed, that the waters will not return, is guaranteed to the whole living order, not to humankind alone.

paragraphs.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת כָּל־בָּשָׂ֛ר ע֖וֹד מִמֵּ֣י הַמַּבּ֑וּל וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד מַבּ֖וּל לְשַׁחֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: I will establish my covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again shall there be a flood to ruin the land.
i18n.he: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת כָּל־בָּשָׂ֛ר ע֖וֹד מִמֵּ֣י הַמַּבּ֑וּל וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד מַבּ֖וּל לְשַׁחֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und ich richte meinen Bund mit euch auf: Nie wieder soll alles Fleisch durch die Wasser einer Flut ausgerottet werden; und nie wieder soll eine Flut sein, um das Land zu verderben.
i18n.es: Estableceré mi pacto con vosotros: nunca más será cortada toda carne por las aguas de un diluvio; nunca más habrá diluvio para arruinar la tierra.
i18n.fr: J'établirai mon alliance avec vous : jamais plus toute chair ne sera retranchée par les eaux d'un déluge ; jamais plus il n'y aura de déluge pour ruiner la terre.
i18n.ja: わたしはお前たちと私の契約を立てる——すべての肉が再び大洪水の水によって絶たれることはなく、地を滅ぼす洪水が再び起こることもない。
i18n.ko: 내가 너희와 내 언약을 세우리라: 모든 육신이 다시는 홍수의 물로 끊어지지 않을 것이며; 다시는 땅을 망치는 홍수가 없으리라.
i18n.ru: И установлю мой завет с вами: не будет больше истреблена всякая плоть водами потопа; и не будет больше потопа, чтобы опустошить землю.
i18n.zh: 我与你们立我的约：一切血肉之躯不再被洪水剪除；也不再有洪水来毁坏大地。
i18n.zh-Hant: 我要與你們立我的約：凡有肉體的，不再被洪水的諸水剪除；也不再有洪水毀壞大地。

notes.official:
**The 'never again' written into the brit.** In 8:21 the never-again promise was internal (*YHWH said in his heart*, an inner resolve). Here in 9:11 it is externalized as a public covenant clause with witnesses. The structure of chapters 8–9 is: first the private divine resolution, then the public divine ratification. The chapter is staging the post-Flood promise twice — first as inward decision, then as outward covenant — and pairing them with the soothing-aroma offering (8:20–21) and the bow-in-the-cloud sign (9:13).

The verb *yikkaret* (shall be cut off) is the technical verb for treaty-violation consequences in the ancient Near East. The chapter is using treaty-vocabulary. The brit is structured like a treaty: parties named, terms specified, sign affixed, witnesses called.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֗ן בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֑ם לְדֹרֹ֖ת עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: The Elohim said: this is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between me and you, and between every living being that is with you, for the generations of forever:
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֗ן בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֑ם לְדֹרֹ֖ת עוֹלָֽם׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sprachen: Dies ist das Zeichen des Bundes, den ich gebe zwischen mir und euch und zwischen jedem lebenden Wesen, das bei euch ist, auf die Generationen der Ewigkeit:
i18n.es: Los Elohim dijeron: esta es la señal del pacto que yo doy entre mí y vosotros, y entre todo ser viviente que está con vosotros, por las generaciones para siempre:
i18n.fr: Les Elohim dirent : voici le signe de l'alliance que je place entre moi et vous, et entre tout être vivant qui est avec vous, pour les générations à perpétuité :
i18n.ja: エロヒムは言われた、「これは、わたしとお前たち、またお前たちと共にいるすべての生ける者との間で、わたしが永遠の世代にわたって与える契約のしるしである。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 말씀하셨다: 이것이 내가 나와 너희 사이에, 그리고 너희와 함께한 모든 산 존재 사이에, 영원한 세대에 걸쳐 주는 언약의 표징이다:
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим: вот знамение завета, который я даю между мною и вами и всяким живым существом, что с вами, на роды вечные:
i18n.zh: 厄罗音说：这是我在我与你们之间，并与你们一同的一切有生命之物之间，所立永世世代之约的记号：
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音說：這就是我所立的約的記號，是在我與你們以及與你們同在的一切生物之間，直到永遠的世代：

notes.official: *Ot ha-brit* — **the sign of the covenant**. The verse introduces the category v13 will fill: a *brit* can carry an *ot*, a perceptible sign that stands for the promise. Genesis and the priestly corpus attach such a sign to three covenants — the bow here, circumcision to Abraham (17:11), and the sabbath as the sign of the creation-rest (Exod 31:17). The bow is the first, and the only one set in the sky rather than on the body or in the calendar: a sign visible to all flesh, matching the all-flesh scope of the covenant it seals.

paragraphs.text: אֶת־קַשְׁתִּ֕י נָתַ֖תִּי בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: My bow I have placed in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of covenant between me and the land.
i18n.he: אֶת־קַשְׁתִּ֕י נָתַ֖תִּי בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Meinen Bogen habe ich in die Wolke gesetzt, und er soll ein Zeichen des Bundes sein zwischen mir und dem Land.
i18n.es: Mi arco he puesto en la nube, y será señal de pacto entre mí y la tierra.
i18n.fr: Mon arc, je l'ai placé dans la nuée, et il sera signe d'alliance entre moi et la terre.
i18n.ja: わたしは私の弓を雲の中に置いた。これがわたしと地との契約のしるしとなるであろう。
i18n.ko: 내가 내 무지개를 구름 가운데 두었으니, 그것이 나와 땅 사이의 언약의 표징이 될 것이다.
i18n.ru: Лук мой я положил в облаке, и будет он знамением завета между мною и землёю.
i18n.zh: 我把我的弓置于云中，它将作为我与大地之间约的记号。
i18n.zh-Hant: 我把我的弓置於雲中，這要作我與大地之間約的記號。

notes.official:
**The bow that hangs in the cloud.** The Hebrew noun is קֶשֶׁת *qeshet* — and elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible it almost exclusively means *war-bow*, the weapon. *Qeshet* is the bow of the warrior (Gen 27:3, 48:22), the bow of YHWH as divine warrior (Hab 3:9, 'you uncovered your bow'), the bow that is broken in eschatological peace texts (Hos 1:5, 2:18, Zech 9:10). The vocabulary is martial.

The chapter's choice to call the rainbow *qeshet* is not casual. The same noun that names the weapon that humans use against each other (cf. 5:5's *darosh-edrosh* logic) and that the divine warrior wields against enemies is now declared *hung up*, *placed in the cloud*, pointed (in the iconography of an unstrung bow held against a cloudy sky) *away from the land* and *toward the heavens*. The Elohim is unstringing the weapon.

On the WoH frame: the chapter is preserving an extraordinary image. The post-Flood promise is signed not with an abstract symbol but with an inverted weapon. The Elohim, having used cosmic violence on humanity once, hangs up the bow as a continuous public sign that the violence is over.

Comparative note: similar imagery appears in Mesopotamian flood traditions. In Atrahasis and the Gilgamesh XI flood, the goddess raises her *necklace of lapis lazuli* (the rainbow) and swears never again to forget the destruction. The motif of a celestial colored arc as a post-flood promise-token is shared; the Hebrew chapter has reshaped the lapis necklace into an unstrung war-bow.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֕ה בְּעַֽנְנִ֥י עָנָ֖ן עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנִרְאֲתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּעָנָֽן׃

i18n.en: Whenever I bring a cloud over the land, the bow shall be seen in the cloud.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֕ה בְּעַֽנְנִ֥י עָנָ֖ן עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנִרְאֲתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּעָנָֽן׃
i18n.de: Wenn ich eine Wolke über das Land bringe, soll der Bogen in der Wolke gesehen werden.
i18n.es: Cuando yo traiga una nube sobre la tierra, el arco será visto en la nube.
i18n.fr: Lorsque je ferai venir une nuée sur la terre, l'arc sera vu dans la nuée.
i18n.ja: わたしが地の上に雲をもたらすとき、弓は雲の中に見えるであろう。
i18n.ko: 내가 땅 위에 구름을 가져올 때마다, 그 무지개가 구름 가운데 보일 것이다.
i18n.ru: И будет: когда наведу я облако на землю, явится лук в облаке;
i18n.zh: 我使云彩遮盖大地的时候，弓就要出现在云中。
i18n.zh-Hant: 我使雲彩臨到大地時，虹必出現在雲中。

paragraphs.text: וְזָכַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה ע֤וֹד הַמַּ֙יִם֙ לְמַבּ֔וּל לְשַׁחֵ֖ת כָּל־בָּשָֽׂר׃

i18n.en: And I will remember my covenant which is between me and you and every living being among all flesh; the waters shall never again become a flood to ruin all flesh.
i18n.he: וְזָכַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה ע֤וֹד הַמַּ֙יִם֙ לְמַבּ֔וּל לְשַׁחֵ֖ת כָּל־בָּשָֽׂר׃
i18n.de: Dann werde ich meines Bundes gedenken, der zwischen mir und euch und jedem lebenden Wesen unter allem Fleisch ist; und nie wieder sollen die Wasser zu einer Flut werden, um alles Fleisch zu verderben.
i18n.es: Y me acordaré de mi pacto que está entre mí y vosotros y todo ser viviente entre toda carne; las aguas nunca más se convertirán en diluvio para arruinar toda carne.
i18n.fr: Et je me souviendrai de mon alliance qui est entre moi et vous et tout être vivant parmi toute chair ; les eaux ne deviendront plus jamais un déluge pour ruiner toute chair.
i18n.ja: わたしは、わたしとお前たち、またすべての肉のうちのすべての生ける者との間の私の契約を覚えるであろう。水は再び、すべての肉を滅ぼす洪水となることはない。
i18n.ko: 그러면 내가 나와 너희와 모든 육신 가운데의 모든 산 존재 사이의 내 언약을 기억하리니; 물이 다시는 모든 육신을 망치는 홍수가 되지 않으리라.
i18n.ru: и вспомню мой завет, который между мною и вами и всяким живым существом во всякой плоти; и не будут более воды потопом, чтобы погубить всякую плоть.
i18n.zh: 我便要记念我的约，就是我与你们和一切血肉之躯中有生命之物之间所立的；水不再成为洪水毁坏一切血肉之躯。
i18n.zh-Hant: 我便要記念我的約，就是在我與你們以及一切肉體中各樣生物之間所立的；諸水必不再成為洪水，毀滅一切肉體。

notes.official:
**The Elohim binds the Elohim's own memory.** The verb is *zakharti* — the same root as 8:1's *vayyizkor Elohim et Noach* (*the Elohim remembered Noah*). At the start of the Flood-reversal, divine memory was the act that turned the waters back. Here that same memory is built into the covenant as the function of the sign. The bow is not a memory aid for humans (humans do not need a reminder that they are alive); it is a memory aid the Elohim establishes for the Elohim. Whenever a cloud comes, the bow appears, and the Elohim's covenant-memory is triggered.

The chapter has now established the architecture of biblical covenant memory: a sign is *given* (*natatti* — v13), the sign is *seen* (*nirathah* — v14), the covenant is *remembered* (*vezakharti* — v15). Three verbs, three steps. The same architecture will recur at Sinai (the law on tablets-of-stone as covenant-memory) and in the prophets ('I have remembered my covenant').

paragraphs.text: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וּרְאִיתִ֗יהָ לִזְכֹּר֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֔ים וּבֵין֙ כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The bow shall be in the cloud, and I will see it — to remember the everlasting covenant between the Elohim and every living being among all flesh that is upon the land.
i18n.he: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וּרְאִיתִ֗יהָ לִזְכֹּר֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֔ים וּבֵין֙ כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Der Bogen soll in der Wolke sein, und ich werde ihn ansehen — um des ewigen Bundes zu gedenken zwischen den Elohim und jedem lebenden Wesen unter allem Fleisch, das auf dem Land ist.
i18n.es: El arco estará en la nube, y yo lo veré—para acordarme del pacto eterno entre los Elohim y todo ser viviente entre toda carne que está sobre la tierra.
i18n.fr: L'arc sera dans la nuée, et je le verrai — pour me souvenir de l'alliance éternelle entre les Elohim et tout être vivant parmi toute chair qui est sur la terre.
i18n.ja: 弓は雲の中にあり、わたしはそれを見て——エロヒムと、地にあるすべての肉のうちのすべての生ける者との間の永遠の契約を覚えるであろう」。
i18n.ko: 무지개가 구름 가운데 있을 것이며, 내가 그것을 볼 것이다 — 엘로힘과 땅 위에 있는 모든 육신 가운데의 모든 산 존재 사이의 영원한 언약을 기억하기 위함이다.
i18n.ru: И будет лук в облаке, и увижу его — чтобы вспомнить вечный завет между Элохим и всяким живым существом во всякой плоти, что на земле.
i18n.zh: 弓必在云中，我必看见它——为要记念厄罗音与一切血肉之躯中有生命之物之间所立的永远之约，凡在大地上的。
i18n.zh-Hant: 虹必出現在雲中，我看見—便要記念厄羅音與大地上一切肉體中各樣生物之間永遠的約。

notes.official: *Brit olam* — **an everlasting covenant**. The bow, once seen, prompts the deity to "remember" (see v15) the *perpetual* covenant. The weight falls on permanence, and on whose memory the sign serves: it is not a reminder to humankind to behave but one the deity sets for the deity — "I will see it and remember". The obligation the sign guards runs one way, from the maker toward all flesh, and it is declared to have no end.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־נֹ֑חַ זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲקִמֹ֔תִי בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֥ין כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The Elohim said to Noah: this is the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the land.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־נֹ֑חַ זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲקִמֹ֔תִי בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֥ין כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Und die Elohim sprachen zu Noah: Dies ist das Zeichen des Bundes, den ich aufgerichtet habe zwischen mir und allem Fleisch, das auf dem Land ist.
i18n.es: Los Elohim dijeron a Noé: esta es la señal del pacto que he establecido entre mí y toda carne que está sobre la tierra.
i18n.fr: Les Elohim dirent à Noé : voici le signe de l'alliance que j'ai établie entre moi et toute chair qui est sur la terre.
i18n.ja: エロヒムはノアに言われた、「これが、わたしと地にあるすべての肉との間に立てた契約のしるしである」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 노아에게 말씀하셨다: 이것이 내가 나와 땅 위에 있는 모든 육신 사이에 세운 언약의 표징이다.
i18n.ru: И сказали Элохим Ною: вот знамение завета, который я установил между мною и всякою плотью, что на земле.
i18n.zh: 厄罗音对挪亚说：这就是我在我与大地上一切血肉之躯之间所立约的记号。
i18n.zh-Hant: 厄羅音對挪亞說：這就是我所立的約的記號，是在我與大地上一切肉體之間所立的。

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ בְנֵי־נֹ֗חַ הַיֹּֽצְאִים֙ מִן־הַתֵּבָ֔ה שֵׁ֖ם וְחָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וְחָ֕ם ה֖וּא אֲבִ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem and Ham and Yapheth; and Ham — he is the father of Canaan.
i18n.he: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ בְנֵי־נֹ֗חַ הַיֹּֽצְאִים֙ מִן־הַתֵּבָ֔ה שֵׁ֖ם וְחָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וְחָ֕ם ה֖וּא אֲבִ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃
i18n.de: Die Söhne Noahs, die aus der Arche kamen, waren Schem und Ham und Japhet; und Ham — er ist der Vater Kanaans.
i18n.es: Los hijos de Noé que salieron del arca fueron Sem, Cam y Jafet; y Cam—él es el padre de Canaán.
i18n.fr: Les fils de Noé qui sortirent de l'arche furent Sem, Cham et Japhet ; et Cham — il est le père de Kena'an.
i18n.ja: 箱舟から出てきたノアの息子たちは、セムとハムとヤフェトであった。ハム——彼はカナンの父である。
i18n.ko: 방주에서 나온 노아의 아들들은 셈과 함과 야벳이었다; 그리고 함 — 그는 가나안의 아버지이다.
i18n.ru: И были сыновья Ноя, вышедшие из ковчега: Сим, Хам и Иафет; а Хам — он отец Ханаана.
i18n.zh: 出方舟挪亚的众子是闪、含、雅弗；含——他是迦南的父亲。
i18n.zh-Hant: 從方舟出來的挪亞的兒子們是閃、含、雅弗；含—他是迦南的父親。

notes.official: **The narrator pre-frames the curse.** Note the timing: the chapter names Ham's three brothers, then *immediately* re-identifies Ham as *the father of Canaan* — before any incident has been narrated. The chapter is editorially priming the reader for v25 (the curse on Canaan, not on Ham himself). The phrase *Cham hu avi Kena'an* is repeated in v22, bookending the incident. The chapter is making sure the reader can connect the post-Flood family to the later Israelite-Canaanite political geography: the curse that falls in this scene will explain the conquest narratives later in the Torah.

paragraphs.text: שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה נָֽפְצָ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole land was scattered.
i18n.he: שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה נָֽפְצָ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
i18n.de: Diese drei waren die Söhne Noahs, und von ihnen aus zerstreute sich das ganze Land.
i18n.es: Estos tres fueron los hijos de Noé, y de estos se dispersó toda la tierra.
i18n.fr: Ces trois furent les fils de Noé, et c'est à partir d'eux que toute la terre fut peuplée.
i18n.ja: これら三人がノアの息子たちであり、これらから全地に人々が散らされた。
i18n.ko: 이 셋이 노아의 아들들이었으며, 이들로부터 온 땅이 흩어졌다.
i18n.ru: Эти трое были сыновьями Ноя, и от них рассеялась вся земля.
i18n.zh: 这三个就是挪亚的众子，全地的人都是从这三个人散布出来的。
i18n.zh-Hant: 這三人是挪亞的兒子—全地的人都從這三人散布開來。

notes.official: **From three sons, all nations — and the word for it foreshadows Babel.** The three sons of Noah become the source from which *the whole land was scattered* (*naftzah*, from פוץ *puts*). The verse is the ethnographic bridge to the Table of Nations (chapter 10), which fans the three lines out into the peoples of the known world. The verb is pointed: *puts*, "scatter, disperse", is the same root that will describe the dispersal from Babel (11:8–9), where scattering is a judgment. Here it is stated neutrally, almost as blessing-fulfilment — the land is filled — and the ambiguity of dispersal, gift or sentence, is set up now to be paid off two chapters later.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֥חֶל נֹ֖חַ אִ֣ישׁ הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וַיִּטַּ֖ע כָּֽרֶם׃

i18n.en: Noah, a man of the soil, began — he planted a vineyard.
i18n.he: וַיָּ֥חֶל נֹ֖חַ אִ֣ישׁ הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וַיִּטַּ֖ע כָּֽרֶם׃
i18n.de: Noah, ein Mann des Bodens, fing an — er pflanzte einen Weinberg.
i18n.es: Noé, varón del suelo, comenzó—plantó una viña.
i18n.fr: Noé, homme du sol, commença — il planta une vigne.
i18n.ja: ノアは大地の人として始め——ブドウ畑を植えた。
i18n.ko: 노아는 흙의 사람으로서, 시작하였다 — 그는 포도원을 심었다.
i18n.ru: И начал Ной, муж земли, и насадил виноградник.
i18n.zh: 挪亚是土壤之人，开始——他栽了一个葡萄园。
i18n.zh-Hant: 挪亞是耕地的人，起初栽植了一個葡萄園。

notes.official:
**Noah the second Adam, planting.** The phrase *ish ha-adamah* — *man of the soil* — echoes 2:5's *ein adam la'avod et ha-adamah* (*there was no human to till the soil*) and 4:2's *Qayin hayah oved adamah* (*Cain was a tiller of soil*). Noah is being named as a continuation of the soil-cultivation line. The first human was placed in a garden; the first human's first son was a soil-tiller; the second-first human's first recorded post-Flood act is planting a vineyard. The chapter is tracking an evolving agricultural identity: garden → field → vineyard.

*Vayyachel* — *he began*. Some rabbinic readings (Bereshit Rabbah 36) heard the verb as *vayyachel* from חלל *chalal* (to profane, to make common) — *Noah profaned*. The Hebrew is ambiguous; the chapter does not commit. But the wordplay sits at the start of the scene, and the events of v21 will retroactively color the verb.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מִן־הַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁכָּ֑ר וַיִּתְגַּ֖ל בְּת֥וֹךְ אָהֳלֹֽה׃

i18n.en: He drank of the wine and became drunk, and uncovered himself within his tent.
i18n.he: וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מִן־הַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁכָּ֑ר וַיִּתְגַּ֖ל בְּת֥וֹךְ אָהֳלֹֽה׃
i18n.de: Und er trank vom Wein und ward trunken und entblößte sich in seinem Zelt.
i18n.es: Bebió del vino y se embriagó, y se descubrió dentro de su tienda.
i18n.fr: Il but du vin et s'enivra, et se découvrit à l'intérieur de sa tente.
i18n.ja: 彼はそのぶどう酒を飲んで酔い、その天幕の中で自らを露わにした。
i18n.ko: 그가 그 포도주를 마시고 취하여, 자기 장막 안에서 벗고 있었다.
i18n.ru: И выпил он вина и опьянел, и обнажился в шатре своём.
i18n.zh: 他喝了酒就醉了，在他的帐棚里赤身露体。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他喝了酒便醉了，在自己的帳棚內赤身露體。

notes.official:
**The first drunkenness, the first uncovering.** Three perfect-consecutive verbs in tight sequence — *vayyesht* (and he drank), *vayyishkar* (and he became drunk), *vayyitgal* (and he uncovered himself). The chapter does not condemn the wine, the drink, or the drunkenness directly; it narrates the sequence as fact and then narrates what happens next.

*Vayyitgal* — from גָּלָה *galah*, the same root as *Galilee* and *galut* (exile, uncovering). The reflexive form (hithpa'el) is rare and pointed: *he uncovered himself*. The next verse (v22) speaks of Ham *seeing* — but the chapter narrates Noah *unmaking* his own cover first. The vulnerability is self-induced and accidental, not assault.

The scene rhymes with chapter 3. There: a piece of fruit, a knowing, a discovered nakedness, a covering with fig leaves. Here: a vine's fruit (wine), a stupor, a self-uncovering, a covering with a garment. The chapter is doing a second-Adam pattern in miniature — Noah's vineyard scene as the post-Flood echo of Eden.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֗רְא חָ֚ם אֲבִ֣י כְנַ֔עַן אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יו וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לִשְׁנֵֽי־אֶחָ֖יו בַּחֽוּץ׃

i18n.en: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.
i18n.he: וַיַּ֗רְא חָ֚ם אֲבִ֣י כְנַ֔עַן אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יו וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לִשְׁנֵֽי־אֶחָ֖יו בַּחֽוּץ׃
i18n.de: Ham, der Vater Kanaans, sah die Blöße seines Vaters und erzählte es seinen beiden Brüdern draußen.
i18n.es: Cam, el padre de Canaán, vio la desnudez de su padre, y se lo contó a sus dos hermanos afuera.
i18n.fr: Cham, le père de Kena'an, vit la nudité de son père, et le rapporta à ses deux frères au-dehors.
i18n.ja: カナンの父ハムは、その父の裸を見て、外にいた二人の兄弟に告げた。
i18n.ko: 가나안의 아버지 함이 자기 아버지의 벗은 모습을 보고, 밖에 있는 자기 두 형제에게 알렸다.
i18n.ru: И увидел Хам, отец Ханаана, наготу отца своего и рассказал двум братьям своим снаружи.
i18n.zh: 迦南的父亲含看见他父亲的赤身，就告诉了在外面的两个弟兄。
i18n.zh-Hant: 迦南的父親含看見他父親的裸露，便告訴外面的兩個弟兄。

notes.official:
**The contested verse.** The Hebrew is short, and that brevity is part of the interpretive problem. *Vayyar Cham et ervat aviv* — *Ham saw the nakedness of his father*. *Vayyaged li-shenei echav ba-chutz* — *and he told his two brothers outside*.

Three readings have circulated through the history of interpretation:

1. **Plain reading**: Ham literally saw his father's naked body and gossiped about it to his brothers. The transgression is the *seeing-and-telling* — the violation of Noah's dignity, especially as compared with the brothers' careful aversion in v23. This is the reading most consistent with the chapter's own next-verse demonstration of the *right* response.

2. **Euphemism for sexual assault**: The phrase *ervat aviv* (the nakedness of one's father) functions as a sexual idiom elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible (Lev 18:7–8, 20:11), where it can name sexual contact with the father's wife. Some readers (already in late antique Jewish tradition, e.g. b. Sanhedrin 70a) infer that something worse than a glance occurred. The chapter's text does not say so; the legal idiom is later.

3. **Euphemism for paternal castration**: A minority reading (also in Sanhedrin 70a) extrapolates that Ham injured Noah in some way that prevented him from fathering a fourth son. The text gives no support beyond the heavy curse that follows.

The chapter itself is silent on which reading is correct. What the chapter *does* commit to is that whatever happened, it was sufficient to warrant the curse on Canaan in v25.

The re-identification of Ham as *avi Kena'an* (the father of Canaan) is repeated here for the third time in five verses (vv. 18, 22, 25). The chapter is hammering the genealogical link. Whoever Ham was, what is being set up is the etiology of the people *Canaan* — the indigenous population of the land that Israel would later occupy. The narrative is doing the political work of explaining a future conquest by placing its origin in a primal family scene.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ שֵׁ֨ם וָיֶ֜פֶת אֶת־הַשִּׂמְלָ֗ה וַיָּשִׂ֙ימוּ֙ עַל־שְׁכֶ֣ם שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וַיְכַסּ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶם֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וְעֶרְוַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃

i18n.en: Shem and Yapheth took the garment and laid it on the shoulders of the two of them, and walked backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; their faces were backward, and the nakedness of their father they did not see.
i18n.he: וַיִּקַּח֩ שֵׁ֨ם וָיֶ֜פֶת אֶת־הַשִּׂמְלָ֗ה וַיָּשִׂ֙ימוּ֙ עַל־שְׁכֶ֣ם שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וַיְכַסּ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶם֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וְעֶרְוַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃
i18n.de: Da nahmen Schem und Japhet das Gewand und legten es auf die Schultern der beiden und gingen rückwärts und bedeckten die Blöße ihres Vaters; ihre Angesichter waren rückwärts gewandt, und die Blöße ihres Vaters sahen sie nicht.
i18n.es: Sem y Jafet tomaron el manto y lo pusieron sobre los hombros de ambos, y caminaron hacia atrás, y cubrieron la desnudez de su padre; sus rostros estaban hacia atrás, y la desnudez de su padre no vieron.
i18n.fr: Sem et Japhet prirent le manteau et le posèrent sur leurs épaules à tous deux, et marchèrent à reculons, et couvrirent la nudité de leur père ; leurs visages étaient tournés en arrière, et la nudité de leur père, ils ne la virent pas.
i18n.ja: セムとヤフェトは衣を取って、二人の肩にかけ、後ろ向きに歩いて、その父の裸を覆った。彼らの顔は後ろを向いており、その父の裸を見なかった。
i18n.ko: 셈과 야벳이 옷을 가져다가 그 둘의 어깨에 메고, 뒤로 걸어가서 자기 아버지의 벗은 모습을 덮었다; 그들의 얼굴은 뒤로 향하였고, 자기 아버지의 벗은 모습을 보지 않았다.
i18n.ru: И взяли Сим и Иафет одежду и, положив её на плечи свои, пошли задом и покрыли наготу отца своего; лица их были обращены назад, и наготы отца своего они не видели.
i18n.zh: 闪与雅弗拿了外衣搭在他们两人的肩上，倒退着走进去，遮盖了他们父亲的赤身；他们的脸是向后的，没有看见他们父亲的赤身。

notes.official:
**Ostentatious carefulness as moral demonstration.** The chapter spends a long verse on a small action. The brothers (i) took a garment, (ii) placed it on the shoulders of *both of them* together, (iii) walked *backward* into the tent, (iv) covered their father's nakedness without turning, (v) kept their faces *backward*, and (vi) did not see. Six clauses for one act of covering.

The verbal contrast with v22 is the point. Ham *saw* (*vayyar*) and *told* (*vayyaged*). Shem and Yapheth *placed* (*vayyasimu*), *walked* (*vayelchu*), *covered* (*vaykhasu*), and *did not see* (*lo ra'u*). The chapter is using verb-architecture to do moral commentary without commentary: one brother accumulates verbs of exposure, two brothers accumulate verbs of covering. The narrator's evaluation is in the syntax.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֥יקֶץ נֹ֖חַ מִיֵּינ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה־ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃

i18n.en: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
i18n.he: וַיִּ֥יקֶץ נֹ֖חַ מִיֵּינ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה־ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃
i18n.de: Als Noah aus seinem Wein erwachte, erkannte er, was sein jüngster Sohn ihm getan hatte.
i18n.es: Noé despertó de su vino, y supo lo que su hijo menor le había hecho.
i18n.fr: Noé s'éveilla de son vin, et sut ce que lui avait fait son fils cadet.
i18n.ja: ノアはぶどう酒から覚め、末の息子が彼にしたことを知った。
i18n.ko: 노아가 술에서 깨어, 자기 막내아들이 자기에게 한 일을 알았다.
i18n.ru: И пробудился Ной от вина своего и узнал, что сделал над ним меньший сын его.
i18n.zh: 挪亚从他的酒中醒来，知道他最小的儿子向他所做的。
i18n.zh-Hant: 挪亞從酒中醒來，知道他最小的兒子向他所行的事，

notes.official:
**'His youngest son' — *bno ha-qatan*.** The phrase has produced an old textual puzzle. The chapter has been listing Noah's sons as *Shem, Ham, Yapheth* (vv. 18, 19, 23) — that ordering places Ham as the middle son, not the youngest. Either (a) the listing order is by prominence rather than birth order, with Ham actually the youngest; or (b) the phrase *bno ha-qatan* is doing other work (the diminutive *qatan* can mean 'small' in dignity, not only in age, in some idioms). The Hebrew is not unambiguous. The chapter does not stop to resolve.

*Vayyeda et asher asah lo* — *and he knew what he had done to him*. The verb *yada* (to know) — the same verb that organized Eden in 2:9 (*the tree of the knowing*) and the recognition of nakedness in 3:7 (*and they knew that they were naked*). Noah waking from wine into knowing-what-his-son-did continues the chapter's Eden-rhyme. The first knowing led to the first hiding; the second knowing leads to the first curse-by-a-human.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָר֣וּר כְּנָ֑עַן עֶ֥בֶד עֲבָדִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְאֶחָֽיו׃

i18n.en: He said: cursed be Canaan; a slave of slaves shall he be to his brothers.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָר֣וּר כְּנָ֑עַן עֶ֥בֶד עֲבָדִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְאֶחָֽיו׃
i18n.de: Da sprach er: Verflucht sei Kanaan; ein Knecht der Knechte sei er seinen Brüdern.
i18n.es: Dijo: maldito sea Canaán; siervo de siervos será para sus hermanos.
i18n.fr: Il dit : maudit soit Kena'an ; qu'il soit pour ses frères esclave des esclaves.
i18n.ja: 彼は言った、「カナンは呪われよ。奴隷の奴隷として、彼はその兄弟たちに仕えるであろう」。
i18n.ko: 그가 말하였다: 가나안은 저주를 받으리라; 그의 형제들에게 종들 중의 종이 되리라.
i18n.ru: И сказал: проклят Ханаан; рабом рабов будет он у братьев своих.
i18n.zh: 他说：迦南当受咒诅；他必给他的众弟兄作奴仆中的奴仆。
i18n.zh-Hant: 便說：迦南當受咒詛；他必作他弟兄們奴僕的奴僕。

notes.official:
**The curse skips the offender.** Ham is the one who saw and told. Canaan is the one who is cursed. The chapter does not explain the skip, and the silence has been heavily theologized across the history of interpretation — none of it grounded in the text. What the text gives is the brute political function: the people *Canaan*, whose territory Israel will later occupy, are being preassigned to slave-status to Shem's line (the Israelite line) and Yapheth's line.

*Eved avadim* — *slave of slaves*. The grammatical construct (*construct of intensification*, like *holy of holies*, *song of songs*) is superlative: the lowest possible status. The chapter is installing the political grammar of conquest in a primal-family curse.

The verse has a brutal reception history: in colonial-era Christian readings, the curse-on-Canaan was racialized and repurposed to justify the African slave trade (the so-called 'curse of Ham', stripped of its actual textual referent to Canaan, the people of the southern Levant). The text is not racial; it is regional and political. But the misreading was load-bearing for centuries of racial-religious ideology, and the historical violence is real. WoH commentary will not minimize that reception, and will not minimize the chapter's own ethnocentric framing either: the curse-of-Canaan formula was the Torah's first attempt to give a divinely-sanctioned origin story to its conflicts with neighbors.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּר֥וּךְ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹ֣הֵי שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: He said: blessed be YHWH, Elohim of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to him.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּר֥וּךְ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹ֣הֵי שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃
i18n.de: Und er sprach: Gepriesen sei YHWH, Elohim Schems; und Kanaan sei ihm Knecht.
i18n.es: Dijo: bendito sea YHWH, Elohim de Sem; y sea Canaán siervo suyo.
i18n.fr: Il dit : béni soit YHWH, Elohim de Sem ; et que Kena'an soit son esclave.
i18n.ja: 彼は言った、「セムのエロヒム、YHWHはほめたたえられよ。カナンは彼の奴隷となれ。
i18n.ko: 그가 말하였다: YHWH, 셈의 엘로힘은 송축을 받으시리라; 그리고 가나안은 그에게 종이 되리라.
i18n.ru: И сказал: благословен YHWH, Элохим Сима; и будет Ханаан рабом ему.
i18n.zh: 他说：闪的厄罗音 YHWH 当受称颂；愿迦南给他作奴仆。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他又說：讚美 YHWH—閃的厄羅音；願迦南作他的奴僕。

notes.official: **YHWH is identified as the *elohim of Shem*.** This is the first time in the Torah that YHWH is identified by relationship to a specific human line. Before this, YHWH has been the Elohim of *the* humans (collectively); here YHWH is the *elohei Shem* — *the Elohim of Shem*. The pattern will repeat: *Elohei Avraham* (Elohim of Abraham), *Elohei Yitzchaq* (Elohim of Isaac), *Elohei Yisrael* (Elohim of Israel). The chapter is opening the genealogical bracket inside which the rest of the Torah's covenant theology will operate. The future Israelite line is being demarcated, here, in a blessing on Shem.

paragraphs.text: יַ֤פְתְּ אֱלֹהִים֙ לְיֶ֔פֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּ֖ן בְּאָֽהֳלֵי־שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.ja: エロヒムはヤフェトを広げられよ。彼はセムの天幕に住め。カナンは彼の奴隷となれ」。
i18n.ko: 엘로힘이 야벳을 창대케 하시기를; 그가 셈의 장막 안에 거하기를; 그리고 가나안은 그에게 종이 되리라.
i18n.ru: Да распространят Элохим Иафета; и да обитает он в шатрах Сима; и будет Ханаан рабом ему.
i18n.zh: 愿厄罗音使雅弗扩张；愿他住在闪的帐棚里；愿迦南给他作奴仆。
i18n.zh-Hant: 願厄羅音擴張雅弗；願他住在閃的帳棚裡；願迦南作他的奴僕。

notes.official:
**The name-pun.** *Yapht Elohim l-Yephet* — *may the Elohim enlarge for Yapheth*. The verb *yapht* (from פתה *patah* — to be wide, to open up, to enlarge) is the same root as the name *Yephet* itself. The chapter is folding a wish into a name: *may the wide one widen*. The same naming-by-pun pattern recurs throughout Genesis (Adam from adamah, Hevel from hevel, Yitzchaq from tzachaq, Yisrael from sarah).

*Yishkon b'oholei Shem* — *may he dwell in the tents of Shem*. The clause is grammatically ambiguous: does *he* refer back to Yapheth (Yapheth will dwell in Shem's tents — a peaceful coexistence reading), or does it refer to the Elohim (the Elohim will dwell in Shem's tents — an early sanctuary-theology reading)? Rabbinic readers split. The chapter does not commit. Either way the structural point is that Shem's tents become the privileged location.

notes.official:
**The last antediluvian-scale lifespan.** Noah lives 950 years total — longer than every patriarch in chapter 5 except Methuselah (969) and Yared (962), and 19 years longer than Adam (930). His lifespan straddles the Flood: 600 years before, 350 years after. The chapter closes the second half of his life in a single verse, mirroring the closing formulae of chapter 5 (*and all his days were X years, and he died*).

Noah is the last person in the Torah to live near a millennium. After him, the lifespans contract sharply: Shem lives 600 (11:11), Arpachshad 438 (11:13), and the curve descends until Abraham at 175 (25:7) and Moses at 120 (Deut 34:7). The chapter is setting up the post-Flood lifespan-decay arc that will run for the next two chapters and shape all later patriarchal accounts.

The 120-year ceiling announced in 6:3 does not bind here yet — Noah and his immediate descendants still live far beyond it. The chapter's calendar of life-lengths is a slow descent across generations, not an instant cap.
